note: Faithful rendering of the Sadāprarudita citations with the abbreviation markers handled correctly.

errors.english: the body of the (Tathagata) One Thus Gone is the (Dharmakaya) Truth Body
errors.why: The Tibetan says the Tathāgata's body is born from all the pure (white) qualities; this qualifier is dropped.

fix.find: the body of the (Tathagata) One Thus Gone is the (Dharmakaya) Truth Body
fix.replace: the body of the (Tathagata) One Thus Gone, born from all the pure qualities, is the (Dharmakaya) Truth Body

errors.english: what should and should not be done
errors.why: The gloss explains 'karma' as being of the nature of doing and refraining (commission and omission), not of what ought or ought not to be done.

note: Sound rendering of the faith-stabilising instructions; one dropped qualifier on the Dharmakāya.

errors.english: except for those where it was not said
errors.why: The offense applies only to one who has NOT said 'I will check whether the donor has built or finished it'; the English excludes exactly those cases.

fix.find: except for those where it was not said
fix.replace: only for one who has not said

errors.english: who the actual agent is in this downfall
errors.why: བྱེད་པ་པོ་ཉིད here is the factor or ground that makes the offense (the vihāra being built), not an 'agent' doing it; 'agent/agency' misleads throughout.

note: Generally follows the commentary, but the key exemption clause is inverted and the technical term for the offense's ground is calqued.

errors.english: the name of the holder of the piece
errors.why: དུམ་བུ་འཛིན་པ is a person's proper name (the rival who later conspires against Candra), rendered as a description.
The prince's name is Candra (Zla ba); a Tibetan transliteration plus a gloss is not the convention for a Sanskrit jātaka name.

errors.english: Those who have not generated qualities,
errors.why: The verse says virtue does not lie in birth, and that even when glass takes the sapphire's colour that colour is the sapphire's quality; the English invents 'those who have not generated qualities' and turns the last line into a question.

errors.english: Dawa is captivating and separated from...
errors.why: The plotter says Candra must by any means be separated from (what he has taken); the English makes it a description of Candra.

note: The narrative is followable, but the names are mishandled and the gnomic verses are poorly construed.

errors.english: Like another refers to a comparison made through analogy.
errors.why: Two separate lemma glosses ('of another' = of others; 'like' = comparison by example) are merged into one, losing the first gloss.

note: Accurate lemma-by-lemma rendering of the tigress commentary, apart from one merged gloss.
Follows the argument on 'ascertained' in the trairūpya definition and on anvaya/vyatireka faithfully.

errors.why: The Tibetan says a flawless author, not an erroneous one.

errors.english: Therefore, I utterly reject that, and I have no great interest in it.
errors.why: The author says he has no great eagerness to refute that point thoroughly, not that he rejects it outright.

errors.english: ...It quickly generates intelligence. In regard to what men desire,
errors.why: The entire side is verse, and it is rendered as running prose throughout.

note: Gets the anti-Mīmāṃsā argument broadly, but reverses 'flawless author' and mistranslates compassion.
Faithful rendering of the general and specific characteristics of the Truths and the two kinds of seekers of liberation.
Very literal but follows the commentary's argument on the body and transformations of consciousness without substantive error.

errors.english: for those who are not ill
errors.why: The lemma is 'for the sick', glossed as those struck by illness.

fix.find: for those who are not ill

errors.english: Utilization by a master [note: of the teachings]
errors.why: This is use as an owner (svāmiparibhoga), not use by a master of the teachings.

fix.find: Utilization by a master [note: of the teachings]

errors.why: འགལ་ཚབས་ཅན is duṣkṛta, a minor wrongdoing; calling it a 'grave offense' misstates its gravity.

errors.english: as well as the teacher and the preceptor being as one
errors.why: The Tibetan means fellow monks who share the same teacher or preceptor, who are among those who must nurse the sick.

note: The property-division rules are mostly right, but a lemma is negated and the five kinds of use are misglossed.
